title: AWS Marketplace Private Offer Template Notes (standard terms, discount guardrails, approvals)
content:
Working notes for standardizing AWS Marketplace Private Offers for Redwood Inference (Hosted / Dedicated / Private + add-ons). This is not final legal language; it’s a GTM + Legal + Finance alignment doc to reduce cycle time and avoid one-off terms that break revrec or billing.

Last edited: 2026-02-12 (post sync w/ AWS + Finance/Legal). Owner: Sofia Mendes.

---
1) Goals / non-goals

Goals
- Repeatable private offer templates that align to the new marketplace SKU catalog (v2) and internal billing meters.
- Clear discount guardrails + approval routing so AEs don’t stall on “who can approve what”.
- Minimize custom terms that create revrec ambiguity or engineering work (metering mappings, quota exceptions, etc.).

Non-goals
- Rewriting Redwood MSA/DPA for AWS Marketplace. Private offers are primarily commercial; legal exceptions should be rare.
- Supporting bespoke metering dimensions per customer (we should not do this).

---
2) Where private offers are used (quick decisioning)

Use an AWS private offer when:
- Customer procurement mandates AWS Marketplace purchase and needs negotiated pricing/commit.
- Customer wants annual or multi-year commit (contract dimension) vs purely public PAYG.
- Customer needs PO-backed spend visibility through AWS billing, or wants to draw down from EDP.

Do NOT use AWS private offer when:
- Customer can buy direct and needs data-processing terms that are easier off-marketplace.
- Customer demands highly bespoke SOW-like deliverables (implementation hours, etc.). Consider separate services SOW + marketplace software contract only.

---
3) Standard offer shapes (templates)

Template A — Hosted API Commit (contract) + usage drawdown
- SKU(s): Hosted Core (marketplace), optionally Hosted Premium Support add-on.
- Commercial structure: committed spend amount with drawdown against metered usage (tokens/embeddings/rerank units) billed via AWS.
- Term: 12 months standard.
- Notes: aligns best to customers wanting predictable spend + procurement simplicity.

Template B — Dedicated Capacity Reservation (contract)
- SKU(s): Dedicated Capacity (by size tier) + optional burst add-on.
- Commercial structure: monthly fixed reservation fee via contract dimension; usage above base is either:
  - (preferred) a defined overage dimension, or
  - handled via a separate Hosted usage SKU if that’s how the catalog is modeled.
- Term: 12–24 months typical.
- Notes: requires additional scoping by SE (throughput targets, region, SLA).

Template C — Private Deployment License (contract)
- SKU(s): Private Deployment Platform Fee + optional compliance package.
- Commercial structure: annual platform license fee via contract + optional support tier.
- Term: 12–36 months depending on enterprise process.
- Notes: ensure shared responsibility + deployment prerequisites are attached in listing/security packet; avoid promising features not in the Private package.

Template D — Bridge / Expansion
- Customer already on public listing/PAYG and needs a private offer for commit or to co-term.
- Key risk: double-billing or overlapping entitlements. Must coordinate with billing (Cole/Nadia) + entitlement linking (Chloe/Ethan) to avoid provisioning confusion.

---
4) Discount guardrails (pricing policy for marketplace)

These guardrails are meant to keep deals within finance-approved ranges while retaining flexibility for strategic accounts.

4.1 Baseline discount bands (by product)
Hosted API commit (Template A)
- 0–15%: AE can propose; approvals: Sales leadership only (Stephanie / Lukas depending on region).
- 15–25%: requires CRO (Jordan) + Finance (Laura) approval.
- >25%: requires CRO + Finance + Product sponsor (Evelyn or relevant PM lead) to validate unit economics; Legal review to confirm no pricing most-favored language.

Dedicated capacity (Template B)
- Discounting is primarily via term length and upfront structure, not deep % off.
- 0–10%: Sales leadership + Finance
- 10–20%: CRO + Finance + Dedicated product lead (Lauren Bishop)
- >20%: exec review required; generally avoid unless capacity is pre-allocated or strategic logo.

Private deployment (Template C)
- 0–10%: Sales leadership + Finance
- 10–20%: CRO + Finance + Private product lead (Vivek Kulkarni)
- >20%: requires CFO delegate + Legal; also confirm support burden + implementation requirements.

4.2 Minimums (to avoid noisy small private offers)
- Hosted commit minimum: $25k annual (unless approved exception for lighthouse/strategic partner).
- Dedicated reservation minimum: one base tier reservation (no “tiny” custom reservations).
- Private deployment minimum: platform fee minimum per pricing guidance (see SKU catalog v2; avoid “$0 platform fee” structures).

4.3 Multi-year / co-terming
- Multi-year contracts allowed (up to 36 months) if AWS portal supports the configuration for the selected product type.
- Co-term: allowed; discount should reflect shorter remaining term (do not treat as net-new annual).

4.4 Free credits / trials inside private offers
- Avoid “$0 for first X months” unless explicitly approved by Finance + RevRec (Emily) due to revenue recognition + marketplace invoicing complexity.
- If necessary, prefer:
  - reduced commit amount with documented ramp plan, or
  - separate marketing credits program off-marketplace.

---
5) Standard commercial terms to keep consistent

These are the “default yes” positions. Any exception should be explicitly called out in the approvals request.

5.1 Effective date, start date, end date
- Start date should be within 30 days of offer acceptance (otherwise risk of stale pricing + forecast noise).
- Term: 12 months default; 24+ months requires Finance approval.

5.2 Payment / invoicing
- AWS invoices the customer; Redwood receives payout via AWS Marketplace schedules.
- Do not promise invoice timing beyond “per AWS Marketplace billing”.

5.3 Refunds / cancellation
- Default: no refunds for committed amounts once accepted (consistent with marketplace contract behavior).
- Any refund language must be reviewed by Legal + Finance (revrec implications).

5.4 SLA references
- If customer requires SLA: ensure the purchased SKU includes the appropriate SLA tier. Do not add custom SLA language in private offer notes.
- If asked, point to Redwood’s SLA policy for Dedicated/Private (as referenced in listing + support docs).

5.5 Support routing
- Standard support channels per purchased tier.
- Always include marketplace support contact email and link to onboarding docs.

---
6) What we should NOT customize in private offers (hard “no” list unless exec exception)

- Custom metering dimensions or changing meter names/IDs.
- Custom data retention/residency commitments not already in the published security packet / contract.
- “Unlimited tokens” or uncapped usage offers.
- Non-standard security claims (SOC/ISO language) in offer notes.
- Side letters attached to the AWS private offer (keep in direct contracting if needed).

---
7) Required approvals (who signs what)

Approval routing summary (operational)
1) AE drafts deal terms (customer, SKU(s), term, commit, discount, region, requested start date).
2) Sales leadership approves commercial rationale + forecast category.
3) Finance approves discount band + billing viability.
4) Legal approves template usage / any redlines.
5) RevOps (Isabelle) confirms HubSpot fields + attach offer ID + close plan.
6) Partnerships/Ops submits in AWS portal (or coordinates with whoever holds portal role).

Approvals matrix (quick lookup)
- Standard template, <=15% discount: Sales leadership
- 15–25% discount: Sales leadership + CRO + Finance
- >25% discount: CRO + Finance + Product sponsor + Legal
- Any non-standard refund/cancellation: Finance + Legal + RevRec
- Any language that references security/compliance deliverables: Security sponsor (Naomi or Dr. Aisha) must review

NOTE: If the offer includes Private deployment or compliance add-ons, route to Security/GRC for confirmation that attachments/links match the current published security packet versions.

---
8) Info required to create an AWS private offer (AE checklist)

Customer identifiers
- AWS account ID(s) that will accept the offer
- Buyer contact email (procurement)
- Preferred AWS region(s) for service use (for Dedicated/Private, confirm capacity constraints)

Product configuration
- Selected marketplace SKU(s)
- Contract amount / rate card reference
- Start date, end date
- Any co-term details (existing subscriptions)

Internal fields (must capture in HubSpot)
- Deal type: Marketplace (AWS)
- Offer type: Public / Private
- AWS private offer ID (once created)
- SKU(s) + commit amount
- Approval log / approvers (who + date)

---
9) Notes on attachments / required docs (what AWS expects)

Per AWS conversations, keep offer notes clean; attach references rather than embedding long claims.
- Link to marketplace onboarding guide (subscription -> entitlement -> org provisioning -> first API call).
- Link to security documentation pack index (public/gated as applicable).
- If applicable, link to Dedicated/Private architecture overview and support SLA page.

Avoid attaching internal-only docs (pricing spreadsheets, revrec memos). Provide customer-facing references only.

---
10) Open questions / items to resolve

1) How to represent Hosted “committed spend drawdown” cleanly in AWS portal dimensions without creating confusion with pure PAYG.
- Owner: Cole Summers / Nadia Rahman
- Target: confirm mapping with aws-marketplace-offer-structure Confluence doc.

2) Do we allow a single private offer to bundle Hosted + Dedicated + Compliance add-on, or enforce one primary product per offer?
- Owner: Chris Osei + Jordan Blake
- Consideration: entitlement linking complexity + support expectations.

3) Standard co-term language for customers migrating from legacy listing SKUs.
- Owner: Isabelle Laurent (process) + Emily Stone (revrec)

---
11) Change log

2026-02-12
- Added explicit “no custom meters” and “no custom security claims” guardrails.
- Updated discount approval bands to include product sponsor review >25%.
- Added minimum commit guidance and notes re: free credits.

2026-01-22
- First draft created after early buyer feedback (procurement via marketplace) and internal discussions on offer consistency.

---
Notes to self (Sofia)
- Before finalizing: confirm names/titles for approval routing + who holds AWS partner portal permissions (see INT-779).
- Align wording with PMM “do/don’t” marketplace copy guidance; ensure no competitive claims in legal/commercial notes.
- Validate with RevRec: how to phrase ramp deals without creating implied performance obligations.
